services.name: Green Book Audio Tour
services.desc: Commonly known as the Green Book, it was an essential travel guide for African Americans during segregation in the United States. Victor Hugo Green was born in Manhattan, New York on November 9, 1892. He spent his childhood in Hackensack, New Jersey with his parents and two younger siblings. At age 21, Green began working as a postal carrier, a career he maintained until retiring in 1952. In 1917, he married Alma Duke, and the couple established their home in Harlem, New York. During World War I, Green served as a Supply Sergeant in the 350th Field Artillery of the 92nd Division (also known as the Buffalo Soldiers). services.name: View Exhibit Page
services.desc: The Legacy of Love Exhibit was the kickoff of the Historic Eureka School Centennial Celebration. The exhibit, named after Grace and Mary Elise Love, a mother and daughter who were both educators in Hattiesburg in the late 19th and early 20th Centuries. Both women taught at Eureka School at some point in their careers.
